headline: FDA approves Dawnzera (donidalorsen) for hereditary angioedema prophylaxis
summary: Ionis Pharmaceuticals announced FDA approval of Dawnzera (donidalorsen), the first and only RNA-targeted therapy approved for HAE prophylaxis. Dawnzera is a subcutaneous antisense oligonucleotide dosed once monthly and is the first new HAE prophylaxis class approved in several years.

headline: European Commission approves Dawnzera (donidalorsen) for HAE prophylaxis in EU
summary: The European Commission granted marketing authorisation for Dawnzera (donidalorsen) for the prevention of recurrent HAE attacks in adults, following CHMP positive opinion. Ionis retains EU rights in partnership with Otsuka Pharmaceutical.

headline: NICE recommends garadacimab (Andembry) for prevention of HAE attacks
summary: The UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) issued a positive recommendation for garadacimab (Andembry, CSL Behring) for the prevention of recurrent HAE attacks in adults and adolescents 12 years and older. Decision enables NHS access.
outcome: Full NICE recommendation (TA1101) — NHS access granted

headline: BioCryst completes acquisition of Astria Therapeutics, adds navenibart to HAE portfolio
summary: BioCryst closed its acquisition of Astria Therapeutics, adding navenibart (formerly STAR-0215), a long-acting, monthly subcutaneous plasma kallikrein inhibitor currently in Phase 3 for HAE prophylaxis. BioCryst now holds both an approved on-demand oral agent (Orladeyo) and a late-stage long-acting prophylaxis candidate.

headline: BioCryst licenses navenibart European rights to Neopharmed Gentili for $70M upfront
summary: BioCryst announced an exclusive European licensing agreement with an Irish affiliate of Neopharmed Gentili for navenibart in HAE. BioCryst receives $70M upfront and up to $275M in regulatory and sales milestones, plus tiered royalties of 18–30% on net European sales. Neopharmed Gentili takes commercial lead across major EU markets.
